segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we've got another lesson all about food and eating.
segments.zh: 我叫凯瑟琳，今天我们有另一节课，全都是关于食物和饮食的。

segments.en: So today we're going to talk about all the tools that we use when we're at the table.
segments.zh: 所以今天我们要聊我们在餐桌旁会用到的所有餐具。

segments.en: So what we use when we're eating.
segments.zh: 所以我们吃的时候用什么。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So let's take a listen to today's dialogue and when we come back, we'll talk about some of these words and some of the great phrases you're learning today.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听听今天的对话，当我们回来时，我们将讨论其中的一些词和你今天学习的一些很棒的短语。

segments.en: Honey, can you set the table?
segments.zh: 亲爱的，你能摆好桌子吗？

segments.en: Well, I'm sure.
segments.zh: 嗯，当然。

segments.en: What are we having for dinner?
segments.zh: 我们晚餐吃什么？

segments.en: Do I need to put anything out in particular?
segments.zh: 有什么需要特别摆出来的吗？

segments.en: Well, make sure to put out the pepper and salt shakers.
segments.zh: 好吧，一定要把胡椒粉和盐瓶拿出来。

segments.en: I don't know if your brother is coming tonight, so set an extra place mat just in case.
segments.zh: 不知道你哥哥今晚来不来，为了以防万一，多摆一张餐垫吧。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Should I use the fancy silverware?
segments.zh: 要用那套餐具中比较讲究的刀叉吗？

segments.en: Yeah, go ahead.
segments.zh: 嗯，请吧。

segments.en: Forks, spoons, and knives.
segments.zh: 叉子、勺子和刀。

segments.en: I roasted some meat, so be sure to put out some steak knives as well.
segments.zh: 我烤了一些肉，所以一定要把一些牛排刀也拿出来。

segments.en: I'll also set some cups and saucers for some coffee after dinner.
segments.zh: 我还会摆好杯子和杯碟，方便饭后喝咖啡。

segments.en: Honey, have you seen our soup bowls?
segments.zh: 亲爱的，你见过我们的汤碗吗？

segments.en: They're in the cupboard where you keep the gravy boat and serving dishes.
segments.zh: 在你放酱汁壶和盛菜盘的那个橱柜里。

segments.en: Just be careful because the wine glasses are also there.
segments.zh: 小心，因为酒杯也在那里。

segments.en: Oops.
segments.zh: 哎呀。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now let's take a look at a couple of words in language takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看语言要点中的几个单词。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So our first word is a very important one.
segments.zh: 所以我们的第一个词是一个非常重要的词。

segments.en: You might have heard it before.
segments.zh: 你可能以前听说过。

segments.en: The word is silverware.
segments.zh: 这个词是银器。

segments.en: Okay, silverware.
segments.zh: 好吧，银器。

segments.en: Now this means that it's usually made something that's made out of silver, right?
segments.zh: 现在这意味着它通常是用银制成的，对吧？

segments.en: It could be.
segments.zh: 可能是。

segments.en: Maybe traditionally it's made out of silver, but it doesn't have to be.
segments.zh: 也许传统上它是由银制成的，但它不必是。

segments.en: You could have wooden silverware or other metals.
segments.zh: 也可能是木制的，或者其他金属做的。

segments.en: It's basically the things that you use to eat food with.
segments.zh: 这基本上是你用来吃食物的东西。

segments.en: Okay, so we're going to take this as a category.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们将把它作为一个类别。

segments.en: There are all the tools that we use to eat food with.
segments.zh: 有我们用来吃食物的所有工具。

segments.en: So for example, a fork is a part of a silverware.
segments.zh: 例如，叉子就是银器中的一种。

segments.en: It's a kind of silverware, fork.
segments.zh: 这是一种银器，叉子。

segments.en: A fork is the one that you usually put in your mouth with a piece of lettuce or meat or something.
segments.zh: 叉子是你通常把一块生菜或肉或其他东西放在嘴里的叉子。

segments.en: Okay, so it's pointy.
segments.zh: 好的，所以它很尖。

segments.en: It has like four little points.
segments.zh: 它有四个小点。

segments.en: Now the one that we use to have dessert or to have soup with, we call that a spoon.
segments.zh: 而我们用来吃甜点或喝汤的那种，我们叫它勺子。

segments.en: A spoon, that's right.
segments.zh: 一个勺子，没错。

segments.en: So to eat yogurt or ice cream, you use a spoon.
segments.zh: 所以要吃酸奶或冰淇淋，你用勺子。

segments.en: And finally, to cut things, you use a knife.
segments.zh: 最后，为了切割东西，你用一把刀。

segments.en: Okay, so in the dialogue we saw the plural form, knives, but singular it would be knife.
segments.zh: 好的，所以在对话中我们看到的是复数形式 knives，单数则是 knife。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And sometimes there are foods that are very, very hard to cut.
segments.zh: 有时有些食物很难切割。

segments.en: For example, steak is very hard to cut because it's a tough meat.
segments.zh: 例如，牛排很难切，因为它的肉比较韧。

segments.en: And so in that case, we use a steak knife to cut it.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我们使用牛排刀来切割它。

segments.en: Okay, so we have a knife or a steak knife.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们有一把刀或一把牛排刀。

segments.en: Steak knife more specifically is used to cut meats.
segments.zh: 牛排刀更具体地用于切肉。

segments.en: All right, so these are three kinds or actually four kinds of silverware.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这是三种或实际上四种银器。

segments.en: Of course, there are other kinds, but those are the most important.
segments.zh: 当然，还有其他种类，但这些是最重要的。

segments.en: After that though, we have something that's important for making your food taste better.
segments.zh: 不过，在那之后，我们有一些对让您的食物味道更好的重要东西。

segments.en: So what if I want to add salt or pepper?
segments.zh: 那么如果我想加盐或胡椒怎么办？

segments.en: What are those things called?
segments.zh: 这些东西叫什么？

segments.en: Those are called salt and pepper shakers.
segments.zh: 这些被称为盐和胡椒瓶。

segments.en: We saw them in the dialogue that we need to put out the pepper and salt shakers.
segments.zh: 我们在对话里看到，要摆出胡椒瓶和盐瓶。

segments.en: So the little thing where you keep the salt is called a shaker.
segments.zh: 所以你装盐的那个小瓶子叫 shaker（撒盐瓶）。

segments.en: That's right, because the action, the verb is to shake.
segments.zh: 没错，因为动作，动词是摇晃。

segments.en: That means moving your hand up and down so some salt will fall out onto your food.
segments.zh: 这意味着上下移动你的手，这样一些盐就会掉到你的食物上。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So usually it's only salt and pepper that we keep in these things, in these little shakers.
segments.zh: 所以通常我们只把盐和胡椒装在这些小调味瓶里。

segments.en: But apart from salt and pepper shakers and all the silverware we're putting out, we're also putting out some saucers because we're going to have coffee later on.
segments.zh: 但除了盐和胡椒瓶以及我们摆出来的所有银器，我们还摆出了一些碟子，因为稍后要喝咖啡。

segments.en: Okay, so this normally goes together with cups, cups and saucers, but everyone knows what a cup is.
segments.zh: 好的，所以这通常与杯子、杯子和碟子搭配使用，但每个人都知道杯子是什么。

segments.en: What is a saucer?
segments.zh: 什么是碟子？

segments.en: So a saucer is this little plate that you put under the cup when you're having coffee.
segments.zh: 所以一个碟子是你在喝咖啡时放在杯子下面的这个小盘子。

segments.en: So usually that's where you keep your spoon or maybe the little bag of tea.
segments.zh: 所以通常这就是你存放勺子的地方，或者可能是那小袋茶。

segments.en: Okay, so a saucer is important because it also helps in case you spill some coffee or tea so the coffee or tea doesn't go on the ground, it goes on the plate.
segments.zh: 好的，所以一个碟子很重要，因为它也有助于防止你洒了一些咖啡或茶，这样咖啡或茶就不会掉到地上，它就在盘子里。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So that little plate is called a saucer.
segments.zh: 所以那个小盘子被称为碟子。

segments.en: Now where do we keep all the plates, all the silverware?
segments.zh: 现在我们把所有的盘子，所有的银器都放在哪里？

segments.en: We usually keep them in a cupboard.
segments.zh: 我们通常把它们放在橱柜里。

segments.en: Okay, so you might want to say cupboard because it's cup, C-U-P-B-O-A-R-D.
segments.zh: 好的，所以你可能想把它读成 cup-board，因为它是 cup 加 board，C-U-P-B-O-A-R-D。

segments.en: That's not right.
segments.zh: 那是不对的。

segments.en: The word is pronounced cupboard.
segments.zh: 这个词读作 cupboard。

segments.en: Okay, so even though it may seem like you should pronounce cupboard, the correct pronunciation is cupboard.
segments.zh: 好的，虽然看起来好像应该读成 cup-board，但正确的读法是 cupboard。

segments.en: Cupboard.
segments.zh: Cupboard（橱柜）。

segments.en: Cupboard.
segments.zh: Cupboard（橱柜）。

segments.en: And a cupboard, like you said, is usually in the dining room or the kitchen because it houses, it keeps all of our plates and bowls and sometimes our silverware.
segments.zh: 就像你说的，橱柜通常放在餐厅或厨房里，因为它用来收纳我们所有的盘子和碗，有时还有银器。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay, so actually in the cupboard we also have some other things, dishes.
segments.zh: 其实橱柜里还有一些别的东西——盘子。

segments.en: Specifically we have a gravy boat in there.
segments.zh: 具体来说，里面有一个酱汁壶（gravy boat）。

segments.en: Okay, so I'm not even sure why they call it a boat, but a gravy boat is basically a special dish.
segments.zh: 好吧，我甚至不确定他们为什么叫它船，但酱汁壶基本上是一种特别的器皿。

segments.en: It's like a tall bowl with a spout so you can pour it that keeps gravy.
segments.zh: 它像一个带壶嘴的高碗，有壶嘴方便你倒，是用来盛肉汁的。

segments.en: So gravy is like a liquid or a sauce that goes on top of meat or potatoes.
segments.zh: 所以肉汁就像肉或土豆上的液体或酱汁。

segments.en: I guess it kind of looks like a boat.
segments.zh: 我想它看起来有点像一艘船。

segments.en: Just imagine a boat, but inside it's empty.
segments.zh: 想象一艘船，但里面是空的。

segments.en: So then that's where you put the gravy in.
segments.zh: 那么这就是你把肉汁放进去的地方。

segments.en: You pour it.
segments.zh: 你倒它。

segments.en: You can pour it.
segments.zh: 你可以倒它。

segments.en: All right, and so we can find that.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们可以找到这一点。

segments.en: We can also find serving dishes, which are basically big plates or bowls that we use when we're having dinner at the dinner table to keep, for example, a turkey or a roast.
segments.zh: 我们还能找到盛菜盘，基本上就是我们在餐桌上吃饭时用来盛东西的大盘子或大碗，比如用来盛火鸡或烤肉。

segments.en: And specifically we were also looking for wine glasses.
segments.zh: 具体来说，我们也在寻找酒杯。

segments.en: Well, maybe we weren't looking for them, but they found us because the person getting stuff out of the cupboard dropped some wine glasses.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许我们不是在找它们，倒是它们找上了我们，因为从橱柜里拿东西的人打碎了几只酒杯。

segments.en: These are very, very easy to break.
segments.zh: 这些非常非常容易打破。

segments.en: Wine glasses are basically just glasses that maybe are tall and you drink wine out of them.
segments.zh: 酒杯基本上就是那种可能比较高、用来喝葡萄酒的杯子。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So there are specific type of glass usually used to drink wine.
segments.zh: 所以有特定类型的玻璃通常用来喝酒。

segments.en: So wine glasses, I guess a normal glass that you use to drink maybe juice or water is just called a glass.
segments.zh: 所以酒杯——我猜你用来喝果汁或水的普通杯子，就直接叫 glass。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you can't use a wine glass only when you're drinking wine.
segments.zh: 所以你不能只在喝酒的时候使用酒杯。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we've taken a look at a lot of vocab here, a lot of tools that we use at the dinner table when we're having dinner.
segments.zh: 所以我们在这里看了很多词汇，我们在晚餐时在餐桌上使用了很多工具。

segments.en: So let's listen to the dialogue again and review.
segments.zh: 所以让我们再次听对话并回顾一下。

segments.en: Honey, can you set the table?
segments.zh: 亲爱的，你能摆好桌子吗？

segments.en: Sure.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: What are we having for dinner?
segments.zh: 我们晚餐吃什么？

segments.en: Do I need to put anything out in particular?
segments.zh: 有什么需要特别摆出来的吗？

segments.en: Well, make sure to put out the pepper and salt shakers.
segments.zh: 好吧，一定要把胡椒粉和盐瓶拿出来。

segments.en: I don't know if your brother is coming tonight.
segments.zh: 我不知道你哥哥今晚会不会来。

segments.en: So set an extra place mat just in case.
segments.zh: 所以多摆一个餐垫，以防万一。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Should I use the fancy silverware?
segments.zh: 要用那套餐具中比较讲究的刀叉吗？

segments.en: Yeah, go ahead.
segments.zh: 嗯，请吧。

segments.en: Forks, spoons, and knives.
segments.zh: 叉子、勺子和刀。

segments.en: I roasted some meat, so be sure to put out some steak knives as well.
segments.zh: 我烤了一些肉，所以一定要把一些牛排刀也拿出来。

segments.en: I'll also set some cups and saucers for some coffee after dinner.
segments.zh: 我还会摆好杯子和杯碟，方便饭后喝咖啡。

segments.en: Honey, have you seen our soup bowls?
segments.zh: 亲爱的，你见过我们的汤碗吗？

segments.en: They're in the cupboard where you keep the gravy boat and serving dishes.
segments.zh: 在你放酱汁壶和盛菜盘的那个橱柜里。

segments.en: Just be careful because the wine glasses are also the...
segments.zh: 小心，因为酒杯也是...

segments.en: Oops.
segments.zh: 哎呀。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We're back.
segments.zh: 我们回来了。

segments.en: So now we have four key phrases that we've prepared for you on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 现在我们有四个关键短语，都是在流利表达上为你准备的。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this first phrase is very important, especially as a child.
segments.zh: 所以第一个短语很重要，尤其是小时候。

segments.en: Your mother or father might ask you to do this.
segments.zh: 你的母亲或父亲可能会要求你这样做。

segments.en: The phrase is to set the table.
segments.zh: 这个短语是 set the table（摆好餐桌）。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's a phrasal verb, to set the table.
segments.zh: 所以 set the table 是一个短语动词。

segments.en: And what does it mean if you're asked to set the table?
segments.zh: 如果有人让你 set the table，那是什么意思？

segments.en: It means you will put down the plates and the silverware and the bowls so that everything is prepared for dinner.
segments.zh: 意思是你要摆好盘子、刀叉和碗，把晚餐的一切都准备好。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is actually what we were doing and a complementary phrasal verb to this.
segments.zh: 所以这其实就是我们刚才在做的事，还有一个与之对应的短语动词。

segments.en: When you're setting the table, as you said, you are putting down or putting out the different spoons, knives, dishes, all that stuff.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，当你摆好桌子时，你是在放下或拿出不同的勺子、刀、盘子等等。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So the verbal phrase to put out means to place down or to make sure that you get something out on the table.
segments.zh: 所以短语动词 put out 的意思是放下，或者确保把某个东西摆到桌上。

segments.en: In this case, my mother would usually ask me to put out extra glasses for water.
segments.zh: 在我的情况下，我妈妈通常会让我多摆几个喝水的杯子。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Or don't forget to put out the wine glasses in case we're drinking wine.
segments.zh: 或者不要忘记拿出酒杯以防我们喝酒。

segments.en: It just means to place down.
segments.zh: 它只是意味着放下。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So just remember that we use it because all these things, they're inside the cupboard.
segments.zh: 所以请记住，我们使用它是因为所有这些东西，它们都在橱柜内。

segments.en: So you have to take them out.
segments.zh: 所以你必须把它们拿出来。

segments.en: So you have to put them out on the table.
segments.zh: 所以你必须把它们放在桌子上。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And sometimes we may have a guest or we may need an extra chair or an extra seat because we are having company and the person in dialogue said to set an extra placemat just in case.
segments.zh: 有时我们会有客人，或者需要多一把椅子、多一个座位，因为有人要来，对话里的人就说要多摆一个餐垫以防万一。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So placemat is basically a piece of plastic or maybe fabric that you put in front of a person when they're at the table.
segments.zh: 所以餐垫基本上就是一块塑料或布，在有人坐到餐桌前时放在他面前。

segments.en: So it's on the table and it's something that protects the table.
segments.zh: 所以它在桌子上，它是保护桌子的东西。

segments.en: So it's small.
segments.zh: 所以它很小。

segments.en: Everyone has one and the bowl and the silverware will go on top of that placemat.
segments.zh: 每个人都有一个，碗和刀叉就放在餐垫上面。

segments.en: But it also indicates that that is where someone will sit.
segments.zh: 但这也表明这是某人会坐的地方。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So to set out or to set out an extra placemat means to prepare an extra place for someone else who will be coming.
segments.zh: 所以 set out，或者说 set out an extra placemat，意思是为即将到来的另一个人多准备一个位置。

segments.en: So if you have a guest, for example, you'll set out an extra placemat for him or for her.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，如果您有客人，您将为他或她设置一个额外的餐垫。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we can say set an extra placemat because this is by this we are referring that somebody is going to sit down at the table or you can just simply say set an extra place for someone.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以说 set an extra placemat，意思就是有人要坐到餐桌旁，或者你也可以简单地说 set an extra place for someone。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Set an extra place.
segments.zh: 多摆一个位置。

segments.en: Your older brother is coming home from college tonight.
segments.zh: 你的哥哥今晚要从大学回家。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you set an extra place for him at the table.
segments.zh: 所以你在餐桌上为他设置了一个额外的位置。

segments.en: And well, in this case, we didn't know if the brother was really coming or not.
segments.zh: 好吧，在这种情况下，我们不知道哥哥到底会不会来。

segments.en: So she said just in case.
segments.zh: 所以她说以防万一。

segments.en: This is a great phrase, one that you'll hear all the time.
segments.zh: 这是一个很好的短语，你会一直听到的。

segments.en: It means I'm not sure what the result will be or what the outcome will be.
segments.zh: 意思是我不确定结果会怎样，会有什么样的结果。

segments.en: But in case something happens or just in case we should do this.
segments.zh: 但万一发生了什么事，或者只是为了以防万一，我们应该这样做。

segments.en: So for example, Marco, I think it's going to rain today.
segments.zh: 例如，马可，我想今天会下雨。

segments.en: You should bring an umbrella just in case.
segments.zh: 为了以防万一，你应该带一把雨伞。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is a way of saying you're preventing something.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种表示你在预防万一的说法。

segments.en: You're prepared.
segments.zh: 你准备好了。

segments.en: Maybe if it does rain, you'll have an umbrella just in case.
segments.zh: 也许如果下雨了，你就会有一把雨伞以防万一。

segments.en: Bring your umbrella.
segments.zh: 带上你的雨伞。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a lot of great phrases there.
segments.zh: 所以那里有很多很棒的短语。

segments.en: A lot of vocab.
segments.zh: 很多词汇。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to the dialogue for the last time.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不最后一次听对话。

segments.en: Honey, can you set the table?
segments.zh: 亲爱的，你能摆好桌子吗？

segments.en: Sure.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: What are we having for dinner?
segments.zh: 我们晚餐吃什么？

segments.en: Do I need to put anything out in particular?
segments.zh: 有什么需要特别摆出来的吗？

segments.en: Well, make sure to put out the pepper and salt shakers.
segments.zh: 好吧，一定要把胡椒粉和盐瓶拿出来。

segments.en: I don't know if your brother is coming tonight.
segments.zh: 我不知道你哥哥今晚会不会来。

segments.en: So set an extra placemat just in case.
segments.zh: 所以设置一个额外的餐垫以防万一。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Should I use the fancy silverware?
segments.zh: 要用那套餐具中比较讲究的刀叉吗？

segments.en: Yeah, go ahead.
segments.zh: 嗯，请吧。

segments.en: Forks, spoons, and knives.
segments.zh: 叉子、勺子和刀。

segments.en: I roasted some meat, so be sure to put out some steak knives as well.
segments.zh: 我烤了一些肉，所以一定要把一些牛排刀也拿出来。

segments.en: I'll also set some cups and saucers for some coffee after dinner.
segments.zh: 我还会摆好杯子和杯碟，方便饭后喝咖啡。

segments.en: Honey, have you seen our soup bowls?
segments.zh: 亲爱的，你见过我们的汤碗吗？

segments.en: They're in the cupboard where you keep the gravy boat and serving dishes.
segments.zh: 在你放酱汁壶和盛菜盘的那个橱柜里。

segments.en: Just be careful because the wine glasses are also there.
segments.zh: 小心，因为酒杯也在那里。

segments.en: Oops.
segments.zh: 哎呀。

segments.en: I'll be right back.
segments.zh: 我马上回来。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So talking about dinner and silverware, there are also a couple of other names that we didn't mention.
segments.zh: 所以说到晚餐和银器，还有一些我们没有提到的其他名字。

segments.en: For example, many people refer to ceramic plates as china.
segments.zh: 例如，很多人把陶瓷盘子叫作 china（瓷器）。

segments.en: Yeah, these are usually the fancy kinds of plates and dishes that you have in your house.
segments.zh: 是的，这些通常是你家里比较讲究的盘子和餐具。

segments.en: Obviously, if you have just kind of the cheap ceramics that you can throw away or even paper plates, those aren't very important.
segments.zh: 显然，如果您只有一些可以扔掉甚至纸盘的廉价陶瓷，那么这些都不是很重要。

segments.en: But at a wedding or in a special occasion, a person or a family might receive chinaware, china.
segments.zh: 但在婚礼或特殊场合，一个人或一个家庭可能会收到一套瓷器，也就是 china。

segments.en: And that is very nice, very pretty porcelain plates or just lacquerware.
segments.zh: 那是非常好，非常漂亮的瓷盘或只是漆器。

segments.en: Okay, so you can call it chinaware, which is basically plates that are either very fine ceramic or porcelain, as you said.
segments.zh: 好吧，你可以称之为瓷器，它基本上是非常精细的陶瓷或瓷器的盘子，正如你所说的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Or what was the other word that you said before?
segments.zh: 或者你之前说的另一个词是什么？

segments.en: Lacquerware.
segments.zh: 漆器。

segments.en: Lacquerware is a certain kind of plate or ceramic that has a kind of sheen to it.
segments.zh: 漆器是一种带有光泽的盘子或陶瓷制品。

segments.en: It's very special, kind of basically paint job.
segments.zh: 它很特别，基本上就是上了一层漆。

segments.en: Oh, okay.
segments.zh: 哦，好吧。

segments.en: Yeah, because it's always been kind of strange the fact that a name like china would also now be related to plates.
segments.zh: 是的，因为像 china 这样一个名字现在也和盘子扯上关系，这一直让我觉得奇怪。

segments.en: But apparently, I guess because Chinese porcelain is renowned as being such high quality, I guess this is why now we just have a word for it called china or chinaware.
segments.zh: 但显然，我猜是因为中国瓷器以高品质闻名，所以现在我们才有 china 或 chinaware 这个词。

segments.en: I think it actually has to do with the fact that the Chinese in the old days sold, well, most of the British bought their porcelain from China.
segments.zh: 我认为这实际上与过去的中国人出售的事实有关，嗯，大多数英国人是从中国购买的瓷器。

segments.en: And so it was very, very in vogue, it was very popular.
segments.zh: 所以它非常非常流行，非常受欢迎。

segments.en: And it was basically the only thing that the British wanted.
segments.zh: 这基本上是英国人想要的唯一东西。

segments.en: They just wanted all of this china.
segments.zh: 他们只想要所有这些瓷器。

segments.en: And it became a part of the vocabulary then.
segments.zh: 当时它成为了词汇的一部分。

segments.en: Yeah, it's really strange though that you would call something china.
segments.zh: 是的，不过你会用 china 来称呼一种东西，这真的很奇怪。

segments.en: It's like, I don't know any other country that you call something, you know, like French.
segments.zh: 就像，我不知道还有哪个国家名会被用来称呼某样东西，你知道，比如 French。

segments.en: This is a French or Frenchware.
segments.zh: 这是 French，或者 Frenchware。

segments.en: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我不知道。

segments.en: I can't think of any.
segments.zh: 我想不出任何。

segments.en: Limoges is the name of a city in France and it's a certain kind of ceramics.
segments.zh: 利摩日是法国一座城市的名称，它是某种陶瓷。

segments.en: Oh, there you go.
segments.zh: 哦，你去吧。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So an interesting topic.
segments.zh: 所以一个有趣的话题。

segments.en: There are many other tools that we didn't mention like salad fork and ice cream spoon.
segments.zh: 还有许多我们没提到的餐具，比如沙拉叉和冰淇淋勺。

segments.en: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我不知道。

segments.en: And sometimes if you go to a fancy dinner, you will have maybe three spoons, three knives, three forks and you don't know what to do with it.
segments.zh: 有时如果你去参加一顿讲究的晚餐，面前可能会摆着三把勺子、三把刀、三把叉子，你却不知道该怎么用。

segments.en: Start on the outside and go in.
segments.zh: 从最外侧的开始，一道一道往里用。

segments.en: That's my one recommendation.
segments.zh: 这是我的一项建议。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So we're really curious to know what you have to say.
segments.zh: 所以我们真的很想知道你要说什么。

segments.zh: 访问我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.zh: 如果您有任何问题，您可以将它们留在那里。

segments.zh: 或者如果你想为某一课推荐一个话题，或者有别的想法，都可以告诉我们。

segments.zh: 好的。

segments.zh: 那我们会见到你的。

segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
